text:
Reprints 
Apple ( AAPL ) reclaimed a flat-base buy point on Friday, but the iPhone maker's move came on light volume and the stock has lagged the S&P 500 index over the last few few months, as shown by its declining relative strength line. Meanwhile, while Apple is making a sluggish move into a buy zone, iPhone chipmakers such as Broadcom ( AVGO ), Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ), Qualcomm ( QCOM ), Qorvo ( QRVO ) and others are lagging the S&P 500 as well. 
X If the case for Apple's growth and stock momentum is so strong, why aren't key suppliers coming along? That's been an issue for months, as Apple itself has made little headway vs. the S&P 500. Apple 
Apple rose 1% to 177.09, reclaiming a 176.34 flat-base buy point . That wasn't an especially powerful price gain. Meanwhile, volume was 7% below normal. You want to see trading activity rise at least 40%-50% above average on breakouts and moves into buy zones. 
Apple's RS line, which tracks a stock's performance vs. the S&P 500 index, is well off recent highs. (The RS line is the blue line in the stock charts below.) Friday's 1% stock move, not much more than the S&P 500's 0.7% advance, did little to change that. You want to see a stock's RS line lead or confirm a breakout or move into a buy area. 
Apple's RS line hasn't made headway since early May. Even when Apple briefly broke out on Dec. 18, the stock's RS line was off its prior highs. 
Can Apple's move into buy zone work? If the market continues to power ahead, then there's a good chance that Apple's stock will continue to climb. It's also possible that Apple will begin to outperform the S&P 500 significantly again. 
But investors should try to focus on stocks that will deliver the strongest gains, while minimizing the risk of losses, especially big losses. 
Apple reports earnings on Feb. 1 . Broadcom 
Broadcom is currently in a flat base with a 285.78 buy point. Shares closed Friday at 264.29, below their 50-day moving average . The RS line has fallen to its lowest levels since early July or early May. That reflects a series of flat bases on top of or next to each other without making much headway. IBD'S TAKE: With the market now in a confirmed rally for 100 days , it's can be hard to see who are the true leading stocks and which are in the middle of the pack. See why IBD's relative strength line is so important . Qualcomm 
Qualcomm is an interesting case for two reasons. 
First, the wireless chip giant is in a royalties battle with key customer Apple, as well as related legal and regulatory challenges and probes around the world. Those woes helped send the stock crashing from October 2016 to last September. 
Second, Broadcom is making a now-hostile bid for Qualcomm, so the latter's shares skyrocketed in November. Since peaking in late November, Qualcomm and Broadcom shares have moved in a similar fashion. Then again, so has Skyworks Solutions. 
Qualcomm is in a huge cup-with-handle base. If you prefer, you can view the handle as a flat base on its own. Either way, the buy point would be 69.38. Shares closed Friday at 65.38, finding support at its fast-rising 50-day line. 
But Qualcomm's RS line has lagged badly since late Nov. 24, reflecting the stock's underperformance over that time. Skyworks Solutions 
Skyworks Solutions is in a consolidation essentially next to two prior patterns that had short-lived breakouts. Skyworks has a 117.75 buy point. Shares closed Friday at 101.21, continuing to trade below its 50-day and 200-day line. The 50-day line last week fell below the 200-day, negative technical action known as a bearish cross. 
Meanwhile, the RS line peaked in early June and is now just off its lowest levels in a year. Qorvo 
Qorvo, like Skyworks, is in a consolidation next to a pair of bases with breakouts that soon failed. It's also below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. The RS line is right around the lowest levels in a year after peaking last May. 
Qorvo is in a consolidation with an 81.30 buy point, but has a lot of work to do. Other Apple Chipmakers 
Analog Devices ( ADI ) and Integrated Device Technology ( IDTI ), both seen as iPhone X plays , are both in shallow, short cup bases. The RS lines are lagging, though a powerful stock gain could lift these stocks' RS lines above at least a short-term high from their recent pseudo-handles (they are not proper handles). Keep in mind that the RS lines have basically been flat for a year. Integrated Device's earnings have been spotty.
